backlog.spec: In featurize, replace GetFingerprintAsNumPy with the count variant (gen.GetCountFingerprintAsNumPy) so each bit holds how many times an environment occurs, not just presence. Keep radius 2 and 2048 bits and the rest of the RF unchanged. Counts often carry more signal for logD than bits.
backlog.title: Count-based Morgan fingerprints

backlog.spec: Set RADIUS = 3 (keep 2048 bits, or raise N_BITS to 4096 if the feature set looks saturated). Larger radius captures bigger substructures, which may help lipophilicity contributions from extended fragments. Nothing else changes.
backlog.title: Larger Morgan radius 3

backlog.spec: Compute the full RDKit descriptor set with rdkit.Chem.Descriptors.CalcMolDescriptors for each molecule (replace NaN/inf with 0 and clip extreme values to the training 1st/99th percentiles). Concatenate these ~200 continuous descriptors (MolLogP, TPSA, HBD, HBA, MolWt, rotatable bonds, aromatic ring count, etc.) to the fingerprint matrix before fitting the RF. Descriptors encode polarity and size, which drive logD.
backlog.title: Add RDKit 2D physchem descriptors

backlog.spec: Append the 167-bit MACCS keys (rdkit.Chem.MACCSkeys.GenMACCSKeys) to the Morgan bit vector for each molecule before the RF. MACCS adds coarse functional-group presence features that complement the hashed Morgan bits.
backlog.title: Add MACCS keys

backlog.spec: Build additional count fingerprints with rdFingerprintGenerator.GetAtomPairGenerator and GetTopologicalTorsionGenerator (fpSize 2048 each) and concatenate them with the Morgan counts. These capture long-range atom-pair and path information that Morgan radius-2 misses.
backlog.title: Atom-pair and topological-torsion fingerprints

backlog.spec: Use GetMorganGenerator with includeChirality=True and a second Morgan variant using atomInvariantsGenerator from GetMorganFeatureAtomInvWeights (pharmacophoric feature invariants: donor, acceptor, aromatic, halogen). Concatenate the standard and feature-invariant count vectors. Feature invariants generalize better across unseen scaffolds.
backlog.title: Chirality-aware and feature-invariant Morgan

backlog.spec: Add a small block of hand-written SMARTS count features: carboxylic acid, tetrazole, sulfonic acid or acyl sulfonamide (acidic), aliphatic amine (basic, excluding amides and anilines), quaternary nitrogen, phenol, amide, hydroxyl, and nitro. logD depends strongly on ionization at pH 7.4, so these counts give the model an explicit ionization signal that bits do not encode directly.
backlog.title: Ionization and polarity SMARTS counts

backlog.spec: Before featurizing, strip salts and small counter-ions by keeping the largest fragment (rdMolStandardize.LargestFragmentChooser), and neutralize charges with rdMolStandardize.Uncharger. This removes noise from salt forms in SMILES. Apply the same cleanup to train and test molecules. Fall back to the original molecule if sanitization fails.
backlog.title: Keep the largest fragment and neutralize charges

backlog.spec: Replace the RandomForestRegressor with lightgbm.LGBMRegressor (num_leaves 31, learning_rate 0.05, n_estimators 600, feature_fraction 0.3, bagging_fraction 0.8 with bagging_freq 1, min_child_samples 10, random_state=seed, n_jobs=8) on the same Morgan bit matrix. Gradient-boosted trees often beat RF on fingerprint regression with enough trees.
backlog.title: LightGBM regressor on fingerprints

backlog.spec: Keep the LightGBM model but set objective='l1' (MAE objective), since the score is mean absolute error and L1 fitting targets the conditional median. Use n_estimators around 800 and learning_rate 0.05. Median-targeted training usually lowers MAE more than the default L2 objective on skewed residuals.
backlog.title: LightGBM with L1 objective

backlog.spec: Use catboost.CatBoostRegressor(loss_function='MAE', iterations=1000, learning_rate=0.05, depth=6, random_seed=seed, verbose=0, thread_count=8) on the Morgan count matrix. CatBoost's symmetric trees are robust on high-dimensional sparse binary features and the MAE loss matches the metric.
backlog.title: CatBoost regressor with MAE loss

backlog.spec: Use xgboost.XGBRegressor(objective='reg:absoluteerror', n_estimators=800, learning_rate=0.03, max_depth=6, subsample=0.8, colsample_bytree=0.3, random_state=seed, n_jobs=8) on the fingerprint matrix. This is a further gradient-boosting option with an MAE-consistent objective.
backlog.title: XGBoost with absolute-error objective

backlog.spec: Compute the Tanimoto similarity matrix on binary Morgan fingerprints (K = A·B / (|A| + |B| - A·B) using numpy matrix products on float arrays). Fit sklearn.svm.SVR(kernel='precomputed', C=5, epsilon=0.1) on the train kernel and predict with the test-by-train kernel. Tanimoto-kernel SVR is a strong fingerprint baseline that respects structural similarity.
backlog.title: Tanimoto-kernel support vector regression

backlog.spec: Use the Tanimoto similarity matrix as a precomputed kernel for kernel ridge regression: solve (K + lambda I) alpha = y_centered with lambda around 0.5 using numpy.linalg.solve, and predict test as K_test @ alpha plus the training mean. Centering y first keeps the intercept sensible. This is a closed-form kernel smoother with no extra hyperparameter search.
backlog.title: Gaussian process with Tanimoto kernel

backlog.spec: Train both the existing RandomForestRegressor and a LightGBM regressor on the same features and return the simple average of their test predictions (0.5/0.5). Averaging two different tree learners reduces variance; keep both seeded from the seed argument.
backlog.title: Blend RF with LightGBM

backlog.spec: Inside fit_predict, make 5 inner KFold splits (shuffle, random_state=seed) of the training set. Produce out-of-fold predictions for RF, LightGBM and Tanimoto-kernel SVR, and stack them as 3 features. Fit a non-negative linear regression (sklearn LinearRegression(positive=True)) on those OOF predictions, then refit the base models on the full train set and apply the meta weights to the test-set base predictions.
backlog.title: Stacking with out-of-fold meta-learner

backlog.spec: Build a model on RDKit physchem descriptors only (CalcMolDescriptors, cleaned as NaN to 0 and clipped), not fingerprints. Fit LightGBM on these ~200 continuous features. Descriptor-based models often capture logD trends such as MolLogP and TPSA more directly than bits. Use this as a separate predictor whose output is later blended or stacked.
backlog.title: Descriptor-only gradient boosting

backlog.spec: Compute RDKit Crippen MolLogP for every molecule. Fit the model to the residual y minus a linear fit a + b*MolLogP obtained by least squares on the training set, and add the linear baseline back to the residual prediction on test molecules. Crippen logP is a strong prior for lipophilicity, so modelling the residual lets the forest focus on what logP misses.
backlog.title: Crippen logP as residual baseline

backlog.spec: Keep the RandomForestRegressor but, instead of averaging its trees, take the median of the per-tree predictions for each test molecule (np.median over estimators_ predictions, stacked). The median is robust to outlying trees and aligns with an MAE target. Compute per-tree predictions with a loop over model.estimators_.
backlog.title: Median of RF tree predictions

backlog.spec: Change the RandomForestRegressor criterion to 'absolute_error' so each split minimizes MAE directly. Reduce N_TREES to 200 to control runtime, since this criterion is slower. Keep max_features=0.3 and min_samples_leaf=1. This aligns the tree-growing objective with the scoring metric.
backlog.title: Random forest with absolute-error criterion

backlog.spec: Replace the fixed max_features=0.3 with max_features=0.15 and set min_samples_leaf=2, keeping 300 trees. Smaller feature subsets decorrelate trees more, and a slightly larger leaf reduces overfitting to near-duplicate analogues in the training folds. Change only these two settings.
backlog.title: Tune RF max_features and leaf size

backlog.spec: Before fitting, clip train_y to its 1st and 99th percentiles (computed on the training labels only) to limit the influence of extreme or noisy measurements. Predict on the original scale. Robust target clipping reduces the damage from outliers that inflate MAE-sensitive fits.
backlog.title: Winsorize training targets

backlog.spec: Train sklearn.neural_network.MLPRegressor with hidden_layer_sizes=(512, 128), activation='relu', alpha=1e-3 (L2 weight decay), early_stopping=True with validation_fraction=0.1, max_iter=300, learning_rate_init=1e-3, random_state=seed, on standardized Morgan count features. Neural nets on fingerprints add a different inductive bias for the ensemble. Clip predictions to the training label range.
backlog.title: MLP on fingerprints with weight decay

backlog.spec: Keep the RandomForestRegressor but set bootstrap=True with max_samples=0.7 (subsampling without replacement-like behaviour) and raise N_TREES to 600. Subsampling adds diversity between trees and lowers the variance of the average. Watch the runtime, which should stay well under the 10-minute limit for 15 fits.
backlog.title: Bootstrap fraction and more trees

backlog.spec: Hold out 10% of the training molecules (seeded split) as an internal validation set. Train LightGBM with learning_rate 0.03, up to 3000 rounds, and early stopping of 100 rounds on validation MAE (metric='l1'). Then refit on all training molecules using the best iteration count scaled by 1.1. Adaptive round count avoids under- or over-fitting the fixed budget.
backlog.title: Early-stopped LightGBM with internal validation

backlog.spec: Use LightGBM with learning_rate=0.01 and n_estimators=3000 on the Morgan count matrix, with feature_fraction=0.3, bagging_fraction=0.8, bagging_freq=1, min_child_samples=10 and objective='l1'. A slower learning rate with many rounds typically gives smoother shrinkage and a small gain in MAE. Keep the runtime under budget by using n_jobs=8.
backlog.title: Lower learning rate with more boosting rounds

backlog.spec: Inside fit_predict, train the RF with 3 different random_state values derived from seed (seed, seed+1, seed+2), each with 200 trees, and average their test predictions. This reduces seed-related variance in the returned predictions at the same total tree count as one 600-tree forest. Keep everything else as in the baseline.
backlog.title: Multi-seed bagging of the final model

backlog.spec: Standardize train_y to zero mean and unit variance before fitting, and invert the transform on predictions. Drop fingerprint bits that are constant across the training set (zero variance) before fitting. For tree models the target scaling is neutral, but removing constant features speeds training and reduces noise in feature sampling.
backlog.title: Standardize target and whiten features

backlog.spec: After prediction, clip the returned values to the interval [min(train_y), max(train_y)] (optionally widened by 0.5 on each side). Tree ensembles already stay inside the label range, so this mainly guards blended or linear components against extrapolation spikes on unusual test molecules. It is a cheap safety step on top of any model.
backlog.title: Prediction clipping to label range

backlog.spec: Replace the single Crippen logP linear baseline with a small linear model on several physics terms: Crippen MolLogP, plus the existing SMARTS ionizable counts (carboxylic acid, tetrazole, sulfonic acid, acyl sulfonamide, basic aliphatic amine, quaternary N). Fit y ~ a + b*logP + c_i*count_i by np.linalg.lstsq (or LinearRegression) on the training fold only, subtract that fitted baseline from y, run the existing stack on the residual, and add the baseline back to the test predictions. This mirrors logD = logP minus an ionization penalty at pH 7.4, so the stack starts from a chemically motivated offset and the penalty coefficients are learned rather than hand-set.
backlog.title: Ionization-corrected physics baseline

backlog.spec: Add a fourth stack member: an sklearn SVR with kernel='precomputed' whose kernel is the MinMax (generalized Tanimoto) similarity sum(min(a,b))/sum(max(a,b)) computed on the atom-pair and topological-torsion count blocks (the columns after the Morgan and SMARTS blocks). Use C=5, epsilon=0.1, and the same OOF/meta-learner scheme as the other members. Compute the kernel with vectorized numpy in chunks to stay within memory and time. This gives a kernel on count information, which the bit-based Tanimoto SVR does not use.
backlog.title: MinMax-kernel SVR on count fingerprints

backlog.spec: Append rdkit.Chem.rdMolDescriptors.CalcAUTOCORR2D (192 values) and the rdkit BCUT2D descriptors (Chem.rdMolDescriptors.BCUT2D, 8 values, or Descriptors.BCUT2D_* if available) to the descriptor matrix. Compute them through the existing _DESC_CACHE path so they are only computed once per SMILES, clean NaN/inf to 0, and clip to the training 1st and 99th percentiles as the current descriptors are. These 2D topological autocorrelation features encode atom-property distributions across the graph and are cheap to compute compared with 3D conformers.
backlog.title: Autocorrelation and BCUT-style descriptors

backlog.spec: Remove the runtime bottleneck that has blocked richer stacks. Keep the same 5-fold OOF stacking, but run the five inner fold fits of base_predict concurrently with joblib (Parallel(n_jobs=5, backend='loky')), setting each model's n_jobs to 1 or 2 so the total stays at 8 threads. Also lower RandomForestRegressor to 100 trees with max_samples=0.7 for the inner folds only. The goal is that a job finishes well under 600 s so that extra stack members (such as a second LightGBM with a different seed or colsample) become affordable. Predictions should be unchanged in expectation.
backlog.title: Parallel OOF fits to cut runtime

backlog.spec: In base_predict's LightGBM, switch to a regularized randomized-tree setup: extra_trees=True, min_child_samples=20, reg_lambda=5.0, colsample_bynode=0.5 (in addition to colsample_bytree=0.3), subsample=0.8 with subsample_freq=1, and keep objective='l1' and learning rate 0.05 with 800 rounds. Extra-random split thresholds and stronger leaf and L2 penalties usually reduce variance on small, skeleton-split datasets where the current model overfits chemotype-specific bits. Change only these LightGBM hyperparameters.
backlog.title: Strongly regularized randomized LightGBM

backlog.spec: Instead of using only the final LightGBM prediction as a stack input, take LightGBM predictions at several iteration counts (for example num_iteration=200, 500, 800) via lg.predict(X, num_iteration=k) and feed all three as separate columns to the LinearRegression(positive=True) meta-learner, with the RF and SVR columns. Use the same single 800-round fit so no extra training cost is added. The meta-learner then learns how much early versus late boosting to trust, which acts as a learned shrinkage schedule across the ensemble.
backlog.title: Stacking on staged LightGBM predictions

backlog.spec: Before fitting, remove fingerprint columns (Morgan, atom-pair, topological-torsion, and MACCS if present) that are nonzero in fewer than 3 training molecules, computing the keep-mask from the training fold only and applying it to the test features. This cuts the feature count from about 6,000 to perhaps 2,000 to 3,000 without touching the SMARTS or descriptor blocks. Fewer, better-supported features reduce the random forest's sensitivity to singleton chemotypes and speed up every model, which may also allow more RF trees within the time limit.
backlog.title: Drop rare fingerprint bits

backlog.spec: Use the unlabeled test SMILES in a second pass. First run the full stack as now and get test predictions. Then append the test molecules with these predicted values as extra training rows, weighted by 0.5 via sample_weight in the LightGBM and RF fits and the kernel model (use the existing Tanimoto SVR with a weighted fit where supported, or skip the SVR for pseudo rows), and refit the stack to produce the final predictions. Because the harness scores only the test molecules, this lets the model adapt its neighborhoods to the test chemotypes. Keep the first-pass predictions as a fallback if the second pass fails.
backlog.title: Transductive pseudo-labeling of test molecules

backlog.spec: Add a fourth stack member that is a k-nearest-neighbour regressor on Tanimoto similarity over the Morgan bit block. For each test molecule, take the k=10 most similar training molecules (similarity from the existing tanimoto function), and predict the weighted median of their targets with weights = similarity raised to the power 3. Include its OOF predictions in the stack like the other members. The nearest-neighbour member is cheap, needs no fitting, and captures local analogue series that the boosted trees and the global SVR may smooth over.
backlog.title: Kernel-weighted nearest-neighbour member

backlog.spec: Weight each training molecule by the inverse of its local density in the training fold. Compute, for each training molecule, the number of other training molecules with Morgan Tanimoto similarity above 0.5 (from the existing tanimoto function on the Morgan block), and set weight = 1/(1 + count) normalized to mean 1. Pass these weights as sample_weight to the LightGBM fit and the RF fit inside base_predict. The aim is to stop dense chemical series from dominating the L1 and squared-error fits, improving generalization to unseen scaffolds, which is the scoring regime.
backlog.title: Inverse-density sample weighting

backlog.spec: In fit_predict, replace LinearRegression(positive=True) on the OOF stack matrix with a meta-learner that minimises absolute error. Fit non-negative weights w (one per base model) and an intercept c by minimising sum |y - (oof @ w + c)| using scipy.optimize.linprog (variables split into positive and negative parts, or a simple nonneg constraint) or scipy.optimize.minimize with method 'Powell' started from the least-squares solution. Keep the existing residual-on-logP baseline and the final prediction formula unchanged.
backlog.title: MAE-optimal non-negative meta-learner

backlog.spec: In base_predict, change the first LightGBM member from objective='l1' to objective='huber' with alpha set to 1.0 (the residual scale after the logP baseline is roughly that size). Keep all other parameters, the RF-style second LightGBM member, and the SVR member unchanged. The Huber loss is smooth near zero, which may give steadier leaf values than pure L1 while staying robust to outliers.
backlog.title: Huber objective in the L1 LightGBM member

backlog.spec: In base_predict, train the first LightGBM member with a cosine-decayed learning rate instead of a constant one. Pass callbacks=[lgb.reset_parameter(learning_rate=...)] to fit, where the rate at round i of N=800 is 0.005 + 0.5*(0.1-0.005)*(1+cos(pi*i/N)). Keep the rest of the parameters as they are. The idea is to take large steps early and small, precise steps late, so the late trees refine the L1 fit.
backlog.title: Cosine learning-rate decay for the boosted member

backlog.spec: In base_predict, change the second LightGBM member (currently gradient boosting with subsample 0.8) to boosting_type='dart' with drop_rate=0.1, skip_drop=0.5, and n_estimators reduced to 400 so runtime stays within the 600 s limit. Keep its other settings. DART drops random earlier trees during training, which is a tree-level dropout regulariser that may reduce over-reliance on early splits in the 6000-column feature set.
backlog.title: DART boosting for the second LightGBM member

backlog.spec: Add a fourth stack member in base_predict: an SVR with an RBF kernel fitted to the clipped RDKit descriptor block only (the columns after the fingerprint, SMARTS and count blocks). Standardise those columns with StandardScaler fitted on the training fold, reduce to 40 principal components with PCA(40, random_state=seed), and fit SVR(kernel='rbf', C=3.0, epsilon=0.1, gamma='scale'). Its prediction is added as a fourth column to the oof matrix and the meta-learner is widened accordingly. This is a smooth, non-tree view of the physchem signal.
backlog.title: RBF SVR on PCA-reduced standardized RDKit descriptors

backlog.spec: In fit_predict, split the training set at the median heavy-atom count (Chem.Mol.GetNumHeavyAtoms). Train the existing base_predict stack separately on the small-molecule half and on the large-molecule half, each with its own inner OOF stacking and meta-learner, and route each test molecule to the regime its heavy-atom count falls into. Keep the Crippen-logP residual baseline fitted on the full training set before the split. This is a simple gating mixture of experts that lets each stack specialise on a size range.
backlog.title: Two-regime mixture by molecular size

backlog.spec: In fit_predict, run the inner 5-fold OOF stacking loop (and the subsequent meta-learner fit and full-data prediction) with two different inner KFold random_state values, seed and seed+1000, and average the two final test predictions. This reduces variance caused by the particular inner fold split used to build the OOF matrix. To stay under 600 s for all 15 fits, reduce the LightGBM member to n_estimators=400 while keeping the SVR member unchanged.
backlog.title: Repeated inner-seed stacking averaged for stability

backlog.spec: In featurize, append the RDKit reduced-graph ErG fingerprint (rdReducedGraphs.GetErGFingerprint, which is a fixed-length pharmacophore-type vector of about 315 floats) to the existing feature matrix, computed per molecule with NaN replaced by 0. It describes pharmacophore-type distances without the atom-level hashing used by Morgan, so it is a different view of the molecule. Keep the existing blocks in their current order.
backlog.title: Element-level reduced-graph (ErG) fingerprint block

backlog.spec: In fit_predict, after the logP residual is computed, fit one quick LightGBM (L1 objective, 300 rounds, same features) with 5-fold OOF on the training set. Compute the absolute OOF residuals, and drop the training rows whose absolute residual exceeds 4 times the median absolute residual. Refit the full stack (base_predict OOF, meta-learner and final prediction) on the remaining rows only, and keep all test rows for prediction. This removes likely label noise without touching the test set.
backlog.title: Trimmed-residual training set (robust label cleaning)

backlog.spec: In fit_predict, widen the stacking meta-learner input beyond the base predictions. After the OOF matrix oof of shape (n, 3) is built, append two raw columns: the Crippen logP and the RDKit TPSA value for each training molecule (and the matching columns for test molecules at prediction time). Standardise these two columns with the training mean and std. Fit the meta-learner as a LinearRegression(positive=True) on the base predictions, with the two raw columns entering as plain, unconstrained linear terms, so the stack can correct base-model shrinkage that depends on size and polarity.
backlog.title: Logical features as extra meta-learner inputs

backlog.spec: In fit_predict, replace the random KFold(5, shuffle=True) used to build the out-of-fold matrix `oof` with GroupKFold-style folds keyed on the Murcko scaffold of each training molecule (compute with rdkit.Chem.Scaffolds.MurckoScaffold.MurckoScaffoldSmiles, group by string, and assign whole groups to folds with a seeded shuffle). The outer harness already tests on unseen scaffolds, so the meta-learner should see base-model errors that look like that regime. Keep everything else unchanged: same three base models, same LinearRegression(positive=True) meta-learner, same residual baseline.
backlog.title: Scaffold-grouped inner OOF for the stack

backlog.spec: In base_predict, for the first LightGBM member only, hold out about 15% of the training rows by Murcko scaffold group (seeded), train with eval_set on that hold-out using objective='l1', and early-stop with early_stopping(100) and a cap of N_ESTIMATORS rounds. Refit on all training rows with the best iteration count found (scaled up by 1.1). This picks the number of rounds for an unseen-scaffold regime rather than the random-row regime. Keep the other two members unchanged. Watch the 600 s budget: the early-stop split should reuse the existing fit, not add a new 5-fold loop.
backlog.title: Scaffold-grouped early stopping for the L1 LightGBM member

backlog.spec: Append the Crippen MolLogP value (already computed as Ltr and Lte) as an extra raw column to X and Xte, after the clipped RDKit descriptors. In base_predict, for the L1 LightGBM member only, pass monotone_constraints with +1 on that column and 0 elsewhere, and set monotone_constraints_method='advanced'. Since the residual baseline already removes the linear logP trend, the constraint only needs to stop the trees from learning non-monotone logP responses, which should act as a smoothing regulariser. Keep the rest of the pipeline as is.
backlog.title: Monotone constraint on Crippen logP feature

backlog.spec: Replace the folded 2048-bit Morgan block in featurize with an unfolded count representation. Using rdFingerprintGenerator.GetMorganGenerator with radius 2 and the AdditionalOutput info (or the bitInfo dictionary from GetSparseCountFingerprint), build a vocabulary over the training molecules only, keep substructures seen in at least 3 training molecules, and produce a count matrix indexed by that vocabulary. Test molecules map onto the same vocabulary and unseen keys are dropped. Cap the width at about 3000 columns by keeping the most frequent keys. This removes hash collisions while staying within the RF-free LightGBM and SVR pipeline; the SVR kernel can use the same count matrix with the min-max kernel or the existing Tanimoto form on binarised counts.
backlog.title: Collision-free unfolded Morgan substructure dictionary

backlog.spec: After computing the final stacked prediction for test molecules, compute a correction from the training residuals. Using the Tanimoto matrix on the Morgan block, for each test molecule find its k=5 most similar training molecules (similarity above a small threshold, otherwise no correction). Take the similarity-weighted mean of their out-of-fold residuals (y minus the OOF stack prediction, which is already available from the inner loop) and add a shrunken version of that mean (multiply by 0.5) to the stack output. This is a local error-correction step on top of the global ensemble, and it costs only one extra similarity matrix.
backlog.title: Nearest-neighbour residual correction after stacking

backlog.spec: Inside fit_predict, before the 5-fold OOF loop, fit one LightGBM L1 model (same settings as the existing lg member) on all training rows and read its split-gain feature_importances_. Keep only the top 600 columns by gain, always keeping the SMARTS, physchem and Crippen columns. Apply the same column mask to X and Xte before calling base_predict. The SVR still uses the Morgan block, so keep the first N_BITS columns of the Morgan block inside the kept set so the Tanimoto kernel is unchanged. This shrinks the tree fits and should reduce the noise from the 6000-plus sparse features, with the side benefit of making the 600 s budget easier to meet.
backlog.title: Importance-based feature selection before base models

backlog.spec: Before fitting any model, replace each training target with a shrunken version: for training molecule i, compute its top-k (k=5) Tanimoto neighbours among the other training molecules on the Morgan block, take their similarity-weighted mean target m_i (weights are similarities above 0.4 only; if none, keep y_i), and set y_i' = (1 - lambda) * y_i + lambda * m_i with lambda = 0.2. Use y' for all base models and for the OOF meta-targets, but evaluate nothing on the shrunken labels. The idea is to damp label noise from activity cliffs by pulling labels toward local consensus. Keep the residual baseline computed on the original y.
backlog.title: Tanimoto-neighbour label shrinkage on training targets

backlog.spec: Add a fourth stack member in base_predict: a sklearn ElasticNet (alpha=0.01, l1_ratio=0.3, max_iter=5000) on the standardized combined matrix. Standardise with the training mean and std, computed inside fit_predict on the training fold and applied to the held-out fold, and clip the standardized values to [-5, 5] so rare bits do not explode. Linear models on fingerprints capture additive group contributions that trees approximate poorly, which may add diversity to the stack. Extend the meta-learner input accordingly and keep LinearRegression(positive=True).
backlog.title: Elastic-net linear member on standardized features

backlog.spec: In base_predict, fit the L1 LightGBM member with its init_score set to the out-of-sample Tanimoto-SVR prediction, so the trees model only what the kernel model leaves over. For the training rows, the SVR prediction is taken from the inner fold it belongs to (or from an inner 3-fold SVR fit on the training rows, to avoid leakage); for the test rows, it comes from the SVR fitted on the full training rows. Predict as svr_pred + lgb_residual_pred. Keep the SVR and the RF-style LightGBM members unchanged. This is a hierarchical stack in which the boosted member corrects the kernel model rather than averaging with it.
backlog.title: Boosting from the SVR offset (init_score stacking)

backlog.spec: After the positive least-squares meta-learner produces its output on the OOF matrix, fit a second one-dimensional linear calibration of the meta output against the OOF targets (y_oof on meta_oof, using the inner OOF meta-predictions from a cross-validated fit of the meta-learner). Apply the fitted slope and intercept to the final test-time meta prediction before adding back the logP baseline. This corrects the systematic shrinkage toward the mean that tree ensembles and kernel regressors show on extreme logD values, without changing any base model. Keep the code to about ten lines.
backlog.title: Post-stack calibration with an OOF slope and intercept

incumbent.description: Replace the RandomForestRegressor stack member with a LightGBM regressor (num_leaves 31, 600 trees, feature_fraction 0.3, bagging 0.8 every round, min_child_samples 10) trained on the same feature matrix.

memo: Incumbent is 0.4882 (slot 22), down from 0.7230. What helped: L1 LightGBM (0.6871), stacking diverse members (0.6425), SMARTS counts (0.6226), atom-pair/torsion counts (0.5694), RF on fewer features (0.5190), Crippen logP residual baseline (0.5025), and replacing the RF with a second LightGBM (0.4882). What did not help: MLP (0.8183), kernel ridge (0.5075), XGBoost (0.5087), Morgan radius 3 (0.5095), count Morgan (0.5004), and extra fourth members or meta-features (0.4872 to 0.4886), all within noise (sd about 0.0042). Several full-descriptor and nested-stacking runs crashed on the 600 s limit, so keep changes cheap. The stack looks saturated on current features. Next: replicate 0.4882 once to pin the noise. Then try cheap LightGBM regularization (extra_trees variant reached 0.4868; ErG reached 0.4836/0.4849), combining the two. Add a few selected descriptors (TPSA, MolWt, H-bond counts). Retest chirality-aware Morgan on the new stack.
